comment: Jev-augment candidate catalog for test_affected.py. Each entry: id, covers (what the test observes AND what breaks it — descriptions drive selection recall), command (argv template; {runner}=mbx-or-cargo, {python}=sys.executable), auto_run (false => suggested only, never executed automatically). Keep ids stable; a stale catalog silently degrades recall.

candidates.covers: asserts a catalog of source file paths: every file containing a name-keyed lookup map must be listed with a reason, and every listed path must still exist and still contain such a map; breaks whenever any covered source file is moved, renamed, deleted, or when a new name-keyed map file is added unrecorded
asserts each crate keeps one discoverable entrypoint with named roots beside it; breaks when src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, named root files, or test modules move, rename, or are added across any crate
cross-crate dependency direction and semantic shape rules; reads Cargo.toml manifests and module structure; breaks when crates gain or lose dependency edges
glob imports/reexports/self-imports rules in Rust sources; breaks when crate files with glob or reexport statements move, rename, or are added
crate roots own orchestration not scattered work; reads entrypoint files of every crate; breaks when lib.rs or named roots change shape
semantic-law conformance: proposition/entailment/quotient checks inside validation; breaks when validation crate behavior changes
lib.rs header comments must carry mechanism/justification/provenance; breaks when lib.rs files move, are created, or headers change
integration test files stay organized under named suites; breaks when test files or directories move, rename, or are added in tests/ trees
no model/ or misc catch-all directories collecting unrelated types; breaks when directories are created, moved, or renamed in crate sources
custody/mutation API rules; scans Rust sources for forbidden patterns; breaks when mutation or custody call sites change

diffs per-fixture compile outcomes (checked/rejected + diagnostics) of ~3300 tests/omega fixtures against the pinned corpus_outcomes.json; breaks when any fixture's compile verdict or diagnostics change, or when corpus_outcomes.json is edited
compiles every tests/omega/pass fixture through the checked-compile route; breaks when any pass fixture stops compiling
compiles every tests/omega/fail fixture expecting rejection matching expected.txt fragments; breaks when a fail fixture compiles or its diagnostic wording drifts
compile-checks run-tier fixtures (native execution legs are separate); breaks when run-tier fixtures stop compiling
compiles + executes corpus/native fixtures as real binaries per target and diffs exit codes/outputs across hosts; breaks when native codegen or ABI behavior changes
compiles the maintained samples/cli|gui|uefi projects end-to-end including their bundled std dependency; breaks when a change affects any source pattern or library feature the samples exercise

omega --check on source/library/std/main.omg: fully compiles the bundled standard library package bodies through the package-project route; breaks when resolution, typing, checking, or package preparation changes reject or exhaust the std source surface
module/namespace resolution: case paths, qualified names, bare-name rejection, index visibility in symbol-resolved trees; breaks when name resolution or module surface semantics change
terminal authority policy: receiving-policy classifications, console host, provider authority in checked compilation; breaks when provider or authority semantics change
unit tests inside checked-interpreter: evaluator semantics, execution states/transitions, wire verification, filesystem model; breaks when interpreter behavior changes
unit tests inside the resolver crate: name/namespace resolution, qualified case values, authored selections, scopes; breaks when resolution semantics change
unit tests inside checking: Unit plans, execution/terminal_unit, custody, effect operations; breaks when checking semantics change
proof-contract and semantic validation unit tests: domains, arithmetic policy, proofs; breaks when validation rules change
independent verifier of serialized Terminal Psi including trusted-surface reconstruction and site digests; breaks when Terminal Psi structure, evidence, or trusted-surface rows change
Terminal Psi serialization round-trip encoding/decoding; breaks when Terminal Psi shapes or codec rules change
interprets Terminal Psi directly: execution outcomes of lowered programs; breaks when Terminal Psi execution semantics change
optimization transform semantics: closed-sum dispatch, edge evidence, unit optimizations; breaks when optimization stage behavior changes
package review/admission evidence: install/review flows, review requirements, admission diagnostics; breaks when package evidence or review semantics change
package manager: workspace installs, named workspaces, offline commands, source diffs; breaks when package management or workspace semantics change
build-time evaluation: builder machine interpretation, build.omg evaluation, providers and settlements; breaks when build machine evaluation or provider semantics change
build declaration model: Build machine vocabulary, depend/package/root declarations; breaks when build declaration semantics change

compiler integration test targets: build_config_granted, build_log_facet, build_target_activation, checked_build_machine_identity, evaluated_via_binding, package_compilation_inputs; breaks when compiler/build integration behavior changes
compiler crate unit tests: product selection, report assembly, coordinator behavior; breaks when compiler coordination changes
omega binary CLI: flag parsing, --check/run/audit/install dispatch, report-file behavior; breaks when CLI dispatch or invocation handling changes
lowering unit tests: expression preparation, bindings, attached units, borrowed-view admission; breaks when lowering semantics change
parser unit tests: statement/expression/type parsing; breaks when grammar or parsing behavior changes
Terminal Psi to abstract operations transform tests; breaks when that lowering changes
object/image writers: ELF/PE/Mach-O encoding, installation records, dynamic tags; breaks when image or codec encoding changes
ISA selection/encoding: x86_64 and aarch64 instruction selection, relocations; breaks when instruction selection or encoding changes
native realization unit tests: provider settlements, source imports, object emission, FMA transport refusal; breaks when native realization semantics change
direct execution of run-tier canaries as real binaries on the host (the _runs observation); breaks when compiled-program runtime behavior changes
bootstrap chain hygiene and alpha-beta edge shell gates; breaks when bootstrap rungs, paths, or chain scripts change
python tools/fmt.py --check: whole-workspace rustfmt formatting; breaks when any Rust source is reformatted
mbx clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings: lint over all crates; breaks when any Rust source introduces a lint
mbx nextest run --workspace --lib: all library unit tests (~16k); breaks when any crate's behavior changes
the audited-documentation canary: surfaces retired when absent from the authored corpus; breaks when allowlisted documentation (AGENTS.md, wiki/) drifts from what the corpus declares
proof kernel/admission suites: derivation checking, proof search, certificate validation; breaks when proof semantics or admission rules change
float provider/semantic tests: float operations, meaning, trapping conversions; breaks when float semantics change
release recorder tests: tools/release record coverage, command completeness; breaks when release-record tooling or documentation commands change
foundation crates: symbols, arenas, handles, diagnostics unit tests; breaks when foundation semantics change
